tb21_profile.skill: Compose a correct qemu-system invocation for a legacy guest image (snapshot mode, VNC display :1 on 5901, monitor socket) and keep it running in the background, then front it with nginx and prove the guest reached its desktop.
tb21_profile.domain: QEMU/KVM system emulation, VNC displays and port mapping, QEMU monitor over a UNIX socket, nginx, legacy x86 guest.
tb21_profile.task_form: Configure-a-service: bring up a long-running background process with an exact set of flags and listening endpoints, verified by probing ports, the socket and the guest's screen state.

verifier_notes: No grade looked misassigned here. Worth flagging for the merge: the two TerminalWorld tasks that match the snapshot/base-image idea best (tw_132013, a qcow2 copy-on-write overlay over a backing file, and tw_132009, booting a cloud image with a NoCloud seed) are both FREE in the packet, as are tw_502937 and task_11950 (XFCE plus tightvncserver over VNC). They are ranked in per_source but kept out of final_top10. TMax's task_001082_5357146e and task_001658_f89501cf are also QEMU-shaped and packet-FREE; I dropped them from per_source entirely because TMax had ten better-verified QEMU tasks. NOTE ON GRADES: work/verifier_strength.json was regenerated after work/packets_v2 was built and the two disagree on ~27% of shown candidates (844 of them flip into or out of FREE). Where they disagree I treated a candidate as FREE if EITHER source calls it FREE, so nothing in final_top10 is FREE under either file.

notes: TMax dominates this task and it is not a lexical artifact: it contains a whole cluster of genuine QEMU-plus-VNC-plus-monitor-socket infrastructure tasks (ten of them, mostly ok/strong graded), which is more QEMU system-emulation content than the rest of the pool combined. CalibForge contributes the only boot-a-guest-in-QEMU and build-QEMU-from-source tasks; its other QEMU entries are user-mode cross-compilation and score lower. Terminal-Lego's single real contribution is task_10686 (QEMU netdev syntax) - the rest of its VNC material is remote-desktop configuration with weak or FREE verifiers. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have essentially nothing here; their entries are filler and their low overalls say so.
